sentences.text:
THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
This appeal is filed by the appellant/claimant, seeking enhancement of the compensation.

2. The brief facts of the case are that on 04.10.2010 at about 3.00 p.m., the petitioner was going on Pandavapura Railway Station-Chindagirikoppalu Road to go back to his native after finishing his work.

At that time, the rider of Bajaj Chetak bearing registration No.KA- 11-H-4595 came in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the petitioner, due to the impact, the claimant fell down and sustained injuries over his left leg, both hands and other parts of his body.
Therefore, the claimant has filed the claim petition, seeking compensation.

3. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for the appellant and the learned counsel for the respondent- Insurance Company and perused the records.
4.

The Tribunal after considering the facts and circumstances and evidence on record, has awarded compensation of Rs.2,58,800/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization, under the following heads:
SL.NO. PARTICULARS AMOUNT  (IN.RS.)
 1. Loss of future earning 1,18,800-00

2 . Pain and suffering 50,000-00  3. Medical expenses and 60,000-00  transportation  4. Loss of earning 10,000-00 Sri Ramu vs Sri Subbegowda on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177242876/
2  5. Food, diet, transport and 10,000-00  attendant charges  6.
Future medical expenses 10,000-00  Total 2,58,800-00 5.
Being aggrieved by the lesser quantum of compensation, the present appeal is filed.
6. In the present case, the claimant was aged about 51 years at the time of accident, he was an agriculturist and was also doing cattle rearing business and earning a sum of Rs.10,000/- per month.

The medical records reveals that the claimant has suffered the following injuries:
(i) Fracture of left leg (ii) Fracture on both hands (iii) Tenderness over middle 1/3rd leg area joint (iv) Tenderness over left knee joint and ankle joint (v) 2 cm., shortening of left lower limb.
PW2-doctor has stated that the appellant/claimant has suffered 46% of disability to the left lower limb.
The Tribunal has taken disability at 25% to the whole body.
Looking to the injuries sustained and disabilities suffered by the claimant, the disability taken by the Tribunal is just and proper.
The accident is of the year 2011.
The notional income of the claimant is to be taken at Rs.5,500/- per month as recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authorities.
The appropriate multiplier applicable is '11'.
Therefore, 'loss of earning capacity due to disability' is re-
assessed and quantified as Rs.1,81,500/- (Rs.5,500x25%x11x12).
The same is awarded under the said head.
7. The compensation awarded under the heads 'Pain and Suffering' and 'Medical Expenses' are just and proper.
The same is kept in tact.
8. The Tribunal has awarded a lesser sum of Rs.10,000/- under the head 'Food, diet, transport and attendant charges'.
The same is enhanced to Rs.25,000/-.

9. The compensation of Rs.10,000/- awarded under the head 'loss of income during laid up period'
is on the lesser.
Looking to the injuries suffered by the claimant, he must not have attended to his work for a period of 4 months.
Therefore, a sum of Rs.22,000/- (Rs.5,500x4 months) is awarded under the said head.

Sri Ramu vs Sri Subbegowda on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177242876/
3 10.
The Tribunal has not awarded any compensation under the heads 'Loss of Amenities'.
It is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.35,000/- under the said head.
11. The compensation of Rs.10,000/- awarded under the head 'Future Medical Expenses' is on the lesser side.
The same is enhanced to Rs.25,000/-.

12. Thus, in all, the claimant is entitled for the following compensation :
SL.NO. PARTICULARS AMOUNT  (IN.RS.)
 1. Pain and sufferings 50,000-00

2 . Medical Expenses 60,000-00  3. Loss of Future income 1,81,500-00  4. Loss of income during laid up 22,000-00  period  5. Loss of Amenities 35,000-00  6. Food, diet, transport and 25,000-00  attendant charges  7.
Future Medical expenses 25,000-00
The Tribunal has awarded the compensation of Rs.2,58,800/-, but the appellant/claimant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.3,98,500/-.

Therefore, the appellant/claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.1,39,700/- (Rs.3,98,500 - Rs.2,58,800) along with interest @ 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till its realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.

14. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed-in-part.
ii. The judgment and award passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.1259/2010 dated 22.05.2012 by the Addl.

Senior Civil Judge, MACT, Srirangapatna, is hereby modified holding the claimant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.1,39,700/- along with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
iii. The appellant/claimant is not entitled for interest for the delayed period of 2066 days in filing the appeal.

iv. Costs made easy.
v.

The other observations and findings of the Tribunal Sri Ramu vs Sri Subbegowda on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177242876/
